287-remember-the-alamo.title: Remember The Alamo
287-remember-the-alamo.creator: Amelia E. Barr
287-remember-the-alamo.description: A book by Amelia E. Barr. But what the monks had taken, they kept; and the fort and the soldier followed the priest and the Cross. Ere long, the beautiful Mission became a beautiful city, about which a sort of fame full of romance and mystery gathered.

arxiv-2106-09884.title: Batch Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Deep Auto-Regressive Networks
arxiv-2106-09884.creator: Shibo Li, Robert M. Kirby, Shandian Zhe
arxiv-2106-09884.description: Abstract Bayesian optimization (BO) is a powerful approach for optimizing black-box, expensive-to-evaluate functions. To enable a flexible trade-off between the cost and accuracy, many applications allow the function to be evaluated at different fidelities. In order to reduce the optimization cost while maximizing the benefit-cost ratio, in this paper we propose Batch Multi-fidelity Bayesian Optimization with Deep Auto-Regressive Networks (BMBO-DARN).

arxiv-2108-07813.title: Embedded Topological Semimetals
arxiv-2108-07813.creator: Saavanth Velury, Taylor L. Hughes
arxiv-2108-07813.description: Abstract Topological semimetals, such as Dirac, Weyl, or line-node semimetals, are gapless states of matter characterized by their nodal band structures and surface states. In this work, we consider layered (topologically trivial) insulating systems in D D dimensions that are composed of coupled multi-layers of d d -dimensional topological semimetals.

arxiv-2110-00802.title: Monadicity of localization for Lie super-algebras 𝔤 ​ 𝔩 ​ ( m , n ) \mathfrak{gl}(m,n)
arxiv-2110-00802.creator: Slava Pimenov
arxiv-2110-00802.description: Abstract 0 Introduction One version of Beilinson-Bernstein localization theory for a semisimple algebraic group G can be stated as follows ( [ BK ] , [ BMR ] , [ BN ] ). Let B be a Borel subgroup and N its unipotent radical.

arxiv-2206-09511.title: The Fallacy of AI Functionality Conference: 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 21–24, 2022; Seoul, Republic of Korea 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’22), June 21–24, 2022, Seoul, Republic of Korea Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.114
arxiv-2206-09511.creator: Inioluwa Deborah Raji*, I. Elizabeth Kumar*, Aaron Horowitz, Andrew D. Selbst
arxiv-2206-09511.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Inioluwa Deborah Raji*, I. Elizabeth Kumar*, Aaron Horowitz, Andrew D. Selbst. Deployed AI systems often do not work. They can be constructed haphazardly, deployed indiscriminately, and promoted deceptively. However, despite this reality, scholars, the press, and policymakers pay too little attention to functionality. This leads to technical and policy solutions focused on “ethical” or value-aligned deployments, often skipping over the prior question of whether a given system functions, or provides any benefits at all.

arxiv-2211-07874.title: On the sound velocity bound in neutron stars
arxiv-2211-07874.description: Abstract It has been suggested in the literature that the sound velocity of the nuclear matter v s v_{s} violates the so-called sound velocity bound v s ≤ c / 3 v_{s}\leq c/\sqrt{3} at high density, where c c is the speed of light.

arxiv-2305-04330.title: Affine equivariant Tyler’s M-estimator applied to tail parameter learning of elliptical distributions
arxiv-2305-04330.creator: Esa Ollila, Daniel P. Palomar, Frédéric Pascal
arxiv-2305-04330.description: Abstract We propose estimating the scale parameter (mean of the eigenvalues) of the scatter matrix of an unspecified elliptically symmetric distribution using weights obtained by solving Tyler’s M-estimator of the scatter matrix. The proposed Tyler’s weights-based estimate (TWE) of scale is then used to construct an affine equivariant Tyler’s M-estimator as a weighted sample covariance matrix using normalized Tyler’s weights.

arxiv-2403-17410.title: On permutation-invariant neural networks
arxiv-2403-17410.creator: Masanari Kimura m.kimura@unimelb.edu.au, Ryotaro Shimizu r2shimizu@ucsd.edu, Yuki Hirakawa yuki.hirakawa@zozo.com, Ryosuke Goto ryosuke.goto@zozo.com, Yuki Saito yuki.saito@zozo.com
arxiv-2403-17410.description: Abstract Conventional machine learning algorithms have traditionally been designed under the assumption that input data follows a vector-based format, with an emphasis on vector-centric paradigms. However, as the demand for tasks involving set-based inputs has grown, there has been a paradigm shift in the research community towards addressing these challenges.

arxiv-2407-10024.title: Counting pairs of cycles whose product is a permutation with restricted cycle lengths
arxiv-2407-10024.creator: Miklós Bóna and Boris Pittel
arxiv-2407-10024.description: Abstract . We find exact and asymptotic formulas for the number of pairs ( s , z ) (s,z) of N N -cycles s s and z z such that all cycles of the product s ⋅ z s\cdot z have lengths from a given set of integers.

arxiv-2408-12285.title: Tactile-Morph Skills: Energy-Based Control Meets Data-Driven Learning
arxiv-2408-12285.creator: Anran Zhang, Kübra Karacan, Hamid Sadeghian, Yansong Wu, Fan Wu, Sami Haddadin
arxiv-2408-12285.description: Abstract Robotic manipulation is essential for modernizing factories and automating industrial tasks like polishing, which require advanced tactile abilities. These robots must be easily set up, safely work with humans, learn tasks autonomously, and transfer skills to similar tasks. Addressing these needs, we introduce the tactile-morph skill framework, which integrates unified force-impedance control with data-driven learning.

arxiv-2503-23306.title: Focus Directions Make Your Language Models Pay More Attention to Relevant Contexts
arxiv-2503-23306.creator: Youxiang Zhu, Ruochen Li, Danqing Wang, Daniel Haehn, Xiaohui Liang
arxiv-2503-23306.description: Abstract Long-context large language models (LLMs) are prone to be distracted by irrelevant contexts. The reason for distraction remains poorly understood. In this paper, we first identify the contextual heads, a special group of attention heads that control the overall attention of the LLM.

arxiv-2506-20368.title: On Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev estimates for degenerate Laplacians
arxiv-2506-20368.creator: Pascal Auscher, Khalid Baadi
arxiv-2506-20368.description: Abstract . We establish norm inequalities for fractional powers of degenerate Laplacians, with degeneracy being determined by weights in the Muckenhoupt class A 2 ​ ( ℝ n ) A_{2}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) , accompanied by specific additional reverse Hölder assumptions. This extends the known results for classical Riesz potentials. The approach is based on size estimates for the degenerate heat kernels.

arxiv-2601-05909.title: Auditing Fairness under Model Updates: Fundamental Complexity and Property-Preserving Updates
arxiv-2601-05909.creator: Ayoub Ajarra, Debabrota Basu
arxiv-2601-05909.description: Abstract As machine learning models become increasingly embedded in societal infrastructure, auditing them for bias is of growing importance. However, in real-world deployments, auditing is complicated by the fact that model owners may adaptively update their models in response to changing environments, such as financial markets.

pmc-10603542.title: Creating and sustaining a digital community of practice for quality improvement in South-East Asia during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-10603542.creator: Vikram Datta, Sushil Srivastava, Komal Lalwani, Rahul Garde, Suprabha K Patnaik, Praveen Venkatagiri, Jeena Pradeep, Vidhyadhar Bangal, Harish Pemde, Achala Kumar, Ankur Sooden, Shreeja Vijayan, Kedar Sawleshwarkar, Rajesh Mehta, Neena Raina, Rajesh Khanna, Vivek Singh, Priyanka Singh, Khushboo Saha
pmc-10603542.description: IntroductionEnsuring quality of care in Low and Middle Income countries (LMICs) is challenging. Despite the implementation of various quality improvement (QI) initiatives in public and private sectors, the sustenance of improvements continues to be a major challenge. A team of healthcare professionals in India developed a digital community of practice (dCoP) focusing on QI which now has global footprints.

pmc-11310027.title: Treatment Responses in Histologic Versus Molecular Diagnoses of Lung Rejection
pmc-11310027.creator: A. Zajacova, M. Mackova, K. Halloran, P. Gauthier, J. Balko, M. Guney, D. Rakita, M. Svorcova, J. Kolarik, J. Vachtenheim, J. Pozniak, J. Simonek, L. Fila, R. Lischke, P. F. Halloran, J. Havlin
pmc-11310027.description: Histologic evaluation of allograft biopsies after lung transplantation has several limitations, suggesting that molecular assessment using tissue transcriptomics could improve biopsy interpretation. This single-center, retrospective cohort study evaluated discrepancies between the histology of transbronchial biopsies (TBBs) with no rejection (NR) and T-cell mediated rejection (TCMR) by molecular diagnosis. The accuracy of diagnosis was assessed based on response to treatment.

pmc-11547061.title: Systematic Investigation on Acid-Catalyzed Truncation of N-Acylated Peptoids
pmc-11547061.creator: Ruiqi Piao, Yong-Uk Kwon, José Manuel González Ros
pmc-11547061.description: Peptoids have emerged as a useful alternative to peptides. However, N-acylated peptoids have occasionally undergone truncation at the terminal peptoid unit under acidic conditions. We previously reported on the mechanistic and electronic aspects of the acid-catalyzed truncation of N-acylated peptoids. To gain further insight, we systematically investigated the conformational and electronic effects of the terminal side chains of peptoids.

pmc-11573743.title: Cryosectioning and immunofluorescence of C. elegans reveals endogenous polyphosphate in intestinal endo-lysosomal organelles
pmc-11573743.creator: Ellen Quarles, Lauren Petreanu, Anjali Narain, Aanchal Jain, Akash Rai, Joyful Wang, Bryndon Oleson, Ursula Jakob
pmc-11573743.description: SummaryPolyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous polyanion present throughout the tree of life. While polyP’s widely varied functions have been interrogated in single-celled organisms, little is known about the cellular distribution and function of polyP in multicellular organisms. To study polyP in metazoans, we developed the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans as a model system.

pmc-11574157.title: Endoscopic dilation of small-intestine strictures in Crohn’s disease by balloon-assisted enteroscopy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11574157.creator: Vishali Moond, Vikram Jeet Singh Gill, Sheza Malik, Ameya Kasture, Sandesh Parajuli, Suha Soni, Saurabh Chandan, Arkady Broder, Babu P. Mohan, Douglas Adler
pmc-11574157.description: BackgroundBalloon-assisted enteroscopy (BAE) (both single- and double-balloon enteroscopy) has garnered attention in the treatment of small intestine strictures in patients with Crohn’s disease (CD). This study aimed to evaluate the pooled clinical outcomes of BAE-mediated endoscopic dilation of small intestine strictures in patients with CD.

pmc-11682773.title: Molecular identification of Klebsiella species from pneumonic goats, Iraq
pmc-11682773.creator: Hanaa Khaleel Ibraheim, Khadeeja S Madhi, Alyaa Sabti Jasim, Hasanain A J Gharban
pmc-11682773.description: Background:In goats, acute and chronic respiratory infections are often characterized by a rapidly progressing clinical course with little opportunity to develop an effective antibiotic therapy.Aim:This study aimed to identify Klebsiella spp. in pneumonic goats, assess its antibiotic susceptibility, and confirm the molecular phylogenetics of Klebsiella spp.

pmc-11714548.title: Increased Myeloid Progenitor Inhibitory Factor 1 and Dysbiosis in Mild COVID‐19 Patients With No Change in Alzheimer's Disease Markers
pmc-11714548.creator: Vijayasree V Giridharan, Celso Catumbela, Bruno Kluwe‐Schiavon, Camila O. Arent, Laura A. Borba, Margarete D. Bagatini, Zuleide M Ignácio, Lucas C Pedro, Luciane B Ceretta, João Quevedo, Rodrigo Morales, Gislaine Z Reus, Tatiana Barichello
pmc-11714548.description: BackgroundThe persistent neurological symptoms seen in long COVID survivors are attributed to immune system dysfunctions and changes in the microbiome induced by SARS‐CoV‐2 infection. In addition to the initial respiratory manifestations, a significant portion of COVID‐19 patients present with neurodegenerative symptoms.

pmc-12557034.title: 5.K. Round table: A comparison of policies to reduce delayed discharges from hospital in four European countries
pmc-12557034.creator: Organised by: European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies, Nuffield Trust, Chair persons: Astrid Eriksen (Germany), Sarah Reed (UK)
pmc-12557034.description: Delays for patients clinically ready for discharge from hospital to the next point of care are a common health system challenge and hold particular urgency, given the backlogs and waiting times for inpatient services in many countries. Delayed discharges are often a result of inefficiencies and coordination problems between the health and social care systems.

pmc-12562016.title: Hamstring Tendon Grafts for Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction: The Effect of a 180° Twist Angle on Tensile Properties
pmc-12562016.creator: Jure Serdar, Ana Pilipović, Giuseppe Filardo, Slavica Martinović, Anita Galić Mihić, Mihovil Plečko, Ozgur Basal, Tomislav Smoljanović, Hamdy Ibrahim
pmc-12562016.description: Background: Evidence regarding the effects of twisting hamstring tendons on graft properties in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction remains controversial. The objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of a 180° twist on the tensile properties of human hamstring tendon grafts (HTGs).

pmc-13148732.title: Longitudinal Trends and Socioeconomic Disparities in Testicular Torsion and Orchiectomy Spanning the COVID-19 Era: A Pediatric Health Information System Database Study
pmc-13148732.creator: Jordan Walsh, John H Makari, Claudia Berrondo
pmc-13148732.description: Introduction: The impact of COVID-19 on testicular torsion frequency, management, and outcomes remains underexplored, with existing studies showing inconsistent results. This study aims to assess the frequency of testicular torsion, orchiectomy rates, and associated demographic and socioeconomic risk factors before, during, and after the pandemic.Methods: The U.S.

pmc-13369205.title: Performance and statistical evaluation of animal dung–driven microbial fuel cells for simultaneous bio electrochemical conversion and bioremediation of toxic metal-contaminated wastewater
pmc-13369205.creator: Mustapha Omenesa Idris, Abdulrahman Itopa Suleiman, Claudia Guerrero-Barajas, Mohamad Nasir Mohamad Ibrahim, Nur Asshifa Md Noh, Dahiru Umar Lawal, Pankaj Sah, Syed Najmul Hejaz Azmi, Mohd Tariq, Parwiz Niazi
pmc-13369205.description: The choice of substrates and their composition play a crucial role in supporting the growth of microorganisms and enhancing overall microbial fuel cells (MFCs) performance. Traditionally used substrates, such as glucose and acetate, are now being replaced by innovative alternatives like biomass materials and food waste.

pmc-13678709.title: Minimally Invasive Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Predominantly Multivessel Coronary Artery Disease: Early Perioperative Outcomes of 149 Patients
pmc-13678709.creator: Dryasir Khan, Ali Akbar Zehri, Rana Altaf
pmc-13678709.description: BackgroundMinimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS-CABG) has evolved from single-vessel revascularization to multivessel surgery without median sternotomy. Although favorable outcomes have been reported, experience remains concentrated in specialized centers. This study evaluated the demographic, operative, and early postoperative characteristics of patients undergoing MICS-CABG, off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OP-CABG) at a single institution.
